question: gfr.38 (dynamic render scale in Live and Build) is finished and tested on macOS. A play test forces heavy frames, the scale drops and stops at min_scale, and the log prints 'render scale at floor: 0.50'. Criterion 3 asks for this run on Windows, and this engine has no Windows machine, so the review keeps sending it back. Options: (A) Accept the macOS run now and file the Windows run as its own bead (cost: Windows proof comes later). (B) Keep the task open until you run `just unity-play-tests RenderScalePlayTests` on the Windows PC and copy client/Logs/unity-play-tests.log into .task/lifesim-gfr.38/evidence/ (cost: it waits for you). (C) Change criterion 3 to say 'a play run' with no platform (cost: Windows is never proven for this feature). I recommend A.

options.label: Accept macOS, file Windows bead
options.answer: Accept the macOS play run as proof for criterion 3 now; the Windows run is a follow-up bead (the leftover), not a blocker for this PR.
options.note: The Windows proof comes later, in its own bead

options.label: Wait for my Windows run
options.answer: Keep criterion 3 as written. I will run `just unity-play-tests RenderScalePlayTests` on the Windows PC and put the log in .task/lifesim-gfr.38/evidence/unity-play-tests-windows.log; check for the floor line there.
options.note: The task waits until the owner runs the test on Windows

options.label: Drop 'Windows' from criterion
options.answer: Criterion 3 becomes 'a play run with a forced heavy frame shows the scale drop and stop at min_scale (log line)'; any platform counts and no follow-up is needed.
options.note: Windows is never proven for this feature

title: Apply the render-scale controller in Live and Build (renderer.R2)
